source_name: Posao.crna.gora.me - job portal + business magazine + company directory
why_relevant: Combines a job board with a company address book and business magazine, so a single crawl yields both bank/PSP vacancies and corporate-entity metadata useful for the actor map.

source_name: Careerjet Montenegro - 'posao banka' aggregated vacancy search
why_relevant: Meta-aggregator that indexes multiple ME job boards and company career pages under one query, giving broad recall for bank/PSP vacancies without crawling each board separately; useful as a coverage safety net for postings that only appear on a bank's own site.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore - Karijera (direct bank career page)
why_relevant: Example of a bank publishing vacancies directly (e.g. head of international payment services). Bank-owned career pages are the primary emission point for the job-ad signal; each licensed bank's page should be enumerated from the CBCG bank register and monitored.

source_name: Bankar.me - Konferencije (banking conference/event coverage)
why_relevant: Dedicated conference category of the ME banking trade portal: agendas, panel titles, speaker lists and sponsor names for domestic and regional banking/payments events. Sponsor and speaker lists are a direct map of which vendors are commercially active in ME payments, and panel topics disclose institutional priorities (instant payments, SEPA, cards) months before formal announcements.

source_name: Infintech conference (Tivat, organised by Logate) - agenda and participants
why_relevant: Recurring regional ME fintech/banking conference (nine panels in 2025 on digital transformation, AI, embedded finance, future of banking) organised by Montenegrin IT firm Logate. Its agenda and delegate/sponsor list is the single densest annual snapshot of who sells payments technology into Montenegro.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore - Odbor udruzenja bankarstva i drugih finansijskih organizacija i osiguranja
why_relevant: Chamber of Commerce banking committee: publishes session agendas, minutes, position papers and event announcements naming member institutions. A reliable pointer to sector working groups, upcoming regulatory changes affecting payments, and to further events and actors.

source_name: Udruzenje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) - ubcg.info
why_relevant: The ME banks' association: member list, seminars/education calendar, statements and event coverage. Serves as the actor map for the banking side of the cell and as an announcement channel for sector conferences and training on payments and cards.

source_name: ICT Cortex - ME ICT cluster (fintech/banking technology commentary and events)
why_relevant: Cluster of Montenegrin ICT companies (including firms supplying banks). Member profiles, project write-ups and event pages reveal which local integrators build payment/card/ATM solutions for ME banks - supplier-side intelligence unavailable from procurement records for private banks.

source_name: CBCG FinTech Hub (fintechhub.cbcg.me) - strategy, survey, hackathon
why_relevant: Regulator-run fintech hub publishing the FinTech Strategy 2025-2029, ecosystem overview and a periodic fintech survey ('fintech istrazivanje'), plus hackathon participant lists. Both an award/event channel and a pointer to named ME fintech actors and to regulator priorities for payments and cards.

source_name: International bank-of-the-year awards coverage for Montenegro (Global Finance / Euromoney / The Banker, as reported by ME media)
why_relevant: Annual 'best bank in Montenegro' awards from Global Finance, Euromoney and The Banker, reported locally with supporting figures (e.g. asset size and lending market share cited for CKB). The award write-ups leak balance-sheet and market-share numbers and signal which institutions are investing in digital/card channels.

source_name: Bankar.me pricing/fee journalism (e.g. cost of instant payments in Montenegro)
why_relevant: Sector media periodically compiles cross-bank fee comparisons (instant payments, card fees, ATM withdrawals) in a readable table form, sometimes ahead of or more granularly than the regulator's own comparison pages, and flags pricing moves worth investigating.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro procurement notices
why_relevant: Donor-funded procurement in ME occasionally covers financial-inclusion, digitalisation and payment-infrastructure projects that never appear on the national portal; notices name technical requirements and eligible suppliers.

source_name: Global Public Procurement Database (GPPD) - Montenegro country profile
why_relevant: World Bank-hosted profile describing the ME procurement legal framework, systems and data availability; useful for judging how complete and machine-readable ME tender data is before building a collector, and for locating the authoritative data endpoints.

source_name: TendersInfo / GlobalTenders / TendersOnTime / MontenegroTenders - commercial Montenegro tender feeds incl. contract awards
why_relevant: English-language commercial feeds that mirror ME notices and, importantly, contract AWARDS - useful for supplier identification when the official portal's award section is hard to query. Keyword pages exist for niche categories, indicating an indexed back-end.

source_name: CBCG — Payment Services Provision and Electronic Money Data (English mirror)
why_relevant: English-labelled mirror of the same quarterly card/terminal dataset; gives stable English table names for mapping the Montenegrin column headers, useful for automated normalisation.

source_name: CBCG — Godišnji izvještaj / Macroeconomic Annual Report
why_relevant: Annual macro report typically contains a payment-system chapter with year-end card, ATM and POS counts plus growth commentary — the cleanest annual snapshot and the source most often quoted by media.

source_name: CBCG — Izvještaj o radu CBCG (annual work report)
why_relevant: Operational annual report of the central bank; the payment-system oversight section describes card-scheme/terminal supervision activity, IPS rollout and reporting changes — context that explains breaks in the card/terminal series.

source_name: Službeni list Crne Gore (Official Gazette)
why_relevant: Primary archive for amendments to payment-system reporting rules and the interchange-fee law; the earliest signal that a statistical definition or reporting frequency is about to change.

source_name: CBCG — Vodič za trgovce / Zakon o međubankarskim naknadama (merchant guide, interchange fee law)
why_relevant: Interchange-fee regulation is the key driver of acquiring economics and therefore of POS estate growth and merchant acceptance; the merchant guide names card schemes and acceptance practices in the Montenegrin market.

source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — Montenegro
why_relevant: Annual, internationally comparable ATM and POS-terminal access-point indicators for Montenegro (e.g. ATMs per 100,000 adults: 81.4 in 2020 rising to 88.69 in 2024), sourced from the CBCG itself. Gives peer benchmarking against Serbia/Croatia/Albania that the national series cannot provide.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro FSAP Technical Note & CPSS/CGPSS retail payments assessments
why_relevant: Independent assessment of Montenegro's retail payments and card infrastructure; notably flags data gaps (e.g. no published count of ACTIVE debit/credit cards, and a recommendation to collect ATM/PoS downtime data) — directly calibrates how much the CBCG card series can be trusted for adoption analysis.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — 'Bankar' quarterly journal
why_relevant: Industry association journal carrying practitioner articles on card business, acquiring, contactless and e-commerce in Montenegro, often quoting figures and naming vendors/processors before they appear in official statistics.

source_name: MONSTAT — Uprava za statistiku Crne Gore
why_relevant: National statistical office: adult population and household ICT/e-commerce usage surveys provide the denominators and the demand-side counterpart (share of individuals buying online, using internet banking) needed to turn raw card/terminal counts into penetration metrics. No dedicated card/ATM series of its own was found.
